HARPER-MENDOZA MEDICAL GROUP - DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Patient: Benjamin Lopez DOB: 05/04/1984 Sex: M MRN: 493923
Admit: 12/21/2024 Discharge: 12/21/2024

Principal diagnosis: Benign tumor / polyps with high grade dysplasia
Secondary diagnoses: None

Procedures: Colonoscopy with polypectomy

Hospital course:
Mr. Benjamin Lopez, a 40-year-old male, presented to the Harper-Mendoza Medical Group December 21, 2024, for management of his benign tumor/polyps with high grade dysplasia. This condition was initially diagnosed on June 1, 2015. Mr. Lopez has been under regular follow-up for this condition, with multiple visits documented over the years. 

On the day of admission, Mr. Lopez reported no acute symptoms but was admitted for a scheduled colonoscopy to monitor and manage his polyps. His vital signs were stable with a blood pressure of 127/74 mmHg and a weight of 163 pounds. Physical examination was unremarkable except for the known history of polyps. 

A colonoscopy was performed, which revealed several polyps in the colon. These polyps were successfully removed via polypectomy. Pathological examination of the removed polyps confirmed the presence of benign tumor/polyps with high grade dysplasia, consistent with previous findings. There were no complications during or after the procedure. Mr. Lopez tolerated the procedure well and was discharged home the same day in stable condition.

Discharge medications: 
None specific to the polyps. Routine multivitamin was recommended.

Follow-up:
Mr. Lopez is advised to follow up with Dr. Kristina Harris, Oncology, at the Harper-Mendoza Medical Group in six months for repeat colonoscopy to monitor for recurrence of polyps. He is also encouraged to maintain a healthy lifestyle, including a balanced diet and regular exercise, to reduce the risk of polyp recurrence.

Additional notes:
Throughout his visits, Mr. Lopez has maintained a stable weight and blood pressure. His most recent weights blood pressures from the past visits are as follows:
- December 21, 2024: Weight 163 pounds, BP 127/74 mmHg
- March 8, 2024: Weight 160 pounds, BP 131/66 mmHg
- May 25, 2023: Weight 157 pounds, BP 128/67 mmHg
- August 10, 2022: Weight 155 pounds, BP 139/75 mmHg
- October 26, 2021: Weight 151 pounds, BP 130/75 mmHg
- January 11, 2021: Weight 159 pounds, BP 126/78 mmHg

Mr. Lopez has no family history of significant medical conditions and reports no tobacco or alcohol use. He is compliant with follow-up appointments and has shown good understanding and management of his condition.

In conclusion, Mr. Lopez was discharged in
stable condition after a successful colonoscopy with polypectomy. He will continue to be monitored for any recurrence of polyps and is advised to maintain regular follow-up appointments.

Gould-Mayo Medical Benjamin Lopez (DOB 05/04/1984)

**July 28, 2024**

Dr. Joshua Farley
Gould-Mayo Medical Group
Specialty: Rheumatology

To Whom It May Concern,

I am writing this letter at the request of Mr. Benjamin Lopez, who will be considering life insurance. This letter serves as a comprehensive report of his medical history and current health status.

Mr. Lopez, a 40-year-old male, was seen in our practice today for an annual physical examination. During this visit, he reported no new and stated that he has been feeling well overall. His current weight is 1S3 pounds, and his blood pressure reading was 139/75 mmHg, which is within normal limits.

Mr. Lopez has a documented history of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), diagnosed in June 2005. The lupus involves multiple organ systems, classified under the category "other" due varied manifestations. His lupus is currently controlled with the use of belimumab, which he receives as a 200 mg injection. This medication has been effective in managing his condition, and there have been no significant lupus flares in recent years.

Physical examination at this visit was largely unremarkable with the exception of minor findings which included a slight pallor and minor joint stiffness noted in the wrists and consistent with his known lupus. The rest of the physical examination including cardiovascular, respiratory, and abdominal assessments, was within normal limits. Mr. Lopez's laboratory results, which were reviewed, continue to show no signs of active lupus-related complications.

**September 03, 2023**

Mr. Lopez was seen on September 3, 2023, regarding his ongoing management of Lupus. At this visit, his blood pressure was 130/76 mmHg, and his weight was 157 pounds. Mr. Lopez reported feeling well overall, with no new symptoms. His physical examination showed no active signs of lupus flare, and his overall condition remained stable.

The laboratory results from this visit also showed no abnormalities that would suggest an active lupus flare. His renal function, liver enzymes, and complete blood count were within normal Mr. Lopez continues to take belimumab 200 mg injections, and this medication has been effective in maintaining the controlled state of his lupus.

**October 08, 2022**

On October 8, 2022, Mr. Lopez was seen for a follow-up concerning his Lupus. His blood pressure at that time was 133/78 mmHg, and he weighed 161 pounds. During this visit, Mr. Lopez reported minor fatigue but no significant new symptoms. His physical examination showed si

gns of active lupus flare. Laboratory tests were reviewed and indicated stable lupus control. 

At this visit, Mr. Lopez continued to be on belimumab 200 mg injections, which have been effective in controlling his lupus with organ involvement. His overall condition remained stable, and he was advised to with his current treatment regimen.

Throughout Mr. Lopez’s visits, he has been compliant with his medication and has not reported any significant side effects from belimumab. He maintains regular follow-ups to monitor his lupus and overall health.

In summary, Mr. Lopez's lupus is well-controlled with belimumab, and he has no new significant health concerns. His physical and laboratory results are consistent with controlled lupus. He is in good health, aside from the chronic management of his autoimmune condition.

If you require any additional information, please do not hesitate to contact our office.

Sincerely,

Dr. Joshua Farley 
Gould-Mayo Medical Group
